plate_comment: Selects the main base timing command: injection_timing_main_base_command = injection_timing_main_base_before_override, or the calibrated injection_timing_main_base_override_value when engine_feature_enable_flags bit 4 (16) is set. Its only reader is cm848_calculateMainInjectionTiming, where it is the base term of the sum / highest / lowest (source code 18). (was cm848_selectFuelLimitOverride)
evidence: The body is four lines (copy the calculated word, replace it with the override cal when flag bit 4 is set). The selected word has 3 reads, all in cm848_calculateMainInjectionTiming (the base term next to the coolant / intake / barometric / boost components), so it is not a fuel limit. Cummins e2m block CBL (combustion limits) lines up by offset: CBL_SOI_Cmd 0x01171B08 = 0x40a46e, C_CBL_SOI_Override_Value 0x01171A06 = 0x40523a.

plate_comment: Looks up the minimum and maximum main timing limits (two engine speed x fuel_demand_limit_copy tables) into injection_timing_combustion_minimum_limit and injection_timing_combustion_maximum_limit, adds injection_timing_user_increment (when engine_feature_enable_flags bit 3 (8) is set; injection_timing_user_increment_active_flag = it is not 0) to fuel_correction_output_snapshot and clamps that between the two limits into injection_timing_main_base_before_override. fuel_demand_mode_code records which limit applied (28 = minimum limit, 27 = maximum limit); cm848_calculateMainInjectionTiming turns them into source codes 30 and 29. (was cm848_calculateRpmLoadTables)
evidence: Read in full. RAM dump: minimum 43, maximum 384, reference 68, result 68, fuel_demand_mode_code 25, so 43 <= 68 <= 384. e2m CBL block: CBL_SOI_Max_Limit +0A = 0x40a470, CBL_SOI_Min_Limit +0C = 0x40a472, CBL_SOI_Ref +0E = 0x40a474, SOI_State_Before_CBL +10 = 0x40a476 (it is snapshotted from fuel_demand_mode_code in this function), CBL_User_Incr_Flag +18 = 0x40a47e (description 'enable AND increment not 0' is the flag expression). The two table triples at 0x40523e / 0x4054e8 follow the e2m order C_CBL_SOI_Min (speed axis, fuel axis, table 0x01171C00-0x01171E00) then Max (0x01171F00-0x01172100).

plate_comment: Computes injection_timing_reference_delta_clamped = injection_timing_combustion_reference - main_injection_timing_for_air_handling (the timing reference minus the main timing actually implemented), limited to engine_load_correction_lower_cal .. engine_load_correction_upper_cal, and looks it up in the fuel_demand_correction_scale_axis_cal / _output_cal table into fuel_demand_correction_scale. cm848_applyFuelDemandOffset then adds a second table adjustment to the timing reference. (was cm848_calculateFuelDemandDelta)
evidence: The two operands are timing angles, not loads: engine_load_normalized is the blended output of four rpm x fuel timing maps (e2m CBR_SOI_Ref) and engine_load_normalized_prev is a copy of main_injection_timing_snapshot (disassembly 0x527820 / 0x527830). e2m CBO block: CBO_Delta_SOI +1E = 0x40a536 (this word), C_CBO_Delta_SOI_Min / _Max 0x01171010 / 12 = the two clamp cals 0x405a0c / 0x405a0e, C_CBO_SOI_Adj_Table with its delta axis = fuel_demand_correction_scale_axis_cal / _output_cal.

plate_comment: Crank run state 3 transition handler: the same steps as cm848_engineRunState3Handler (snapshot crank_period_accumulator into crank_period_prev_snapshot, restart engine_event_countdown from its calibration, run_state = 3, leave speed limp home if it is active, re-run engine_injectionTiming_crankSyncDispatch) and additionally latches crank_event_timebase_b = TBLr - timebase_previous_capture the first time it is 0. No protection logic. (was cm848_protectionOverrideEvaluator)
evidence: Read in full (21 lines): no protection, override or evaluation logic. It is cm848_engineRunState3Handler plus the one-time time base latch, in the same family as cm848_engineRunState4Handler / ...Handler2 / ...4Conditional, which latch crank_tooth_period_tbl.

plate_comment: Crank-synchronous injection dispatcher. With engine_speed_limp_home_active_flag = 0 it waits until the TPU-A host service request bits clear, takes the tooth number from TPU-A channel 0 parameter 4, looks up cylinder_event_index and calls cm848_scheduleInjectionAnglesOnPrimarySpeedInput; with the flag = 1 (speed limp home) it takes the tooth number from channel 1 parameter 2 and calls cm848_scheduleInjectionAnglesInSpeedLimpHome. Clears crank_tooth_count_b at the end. (was mpc555_processProtectionConditions; no protection logic)
evidence: Name is right. The current plate still names the old callees schedule_crankValid / schedule_crankInvalid, which are now cm848_scheduleInjectionAnglesInSpeedLimpHome / cm848_scheduleInjectionAnglesOnPrimarySpeedInput; the body (read in full) matches the text above.

plate_comment: Crank state transition handler: sets engine_crank_state.crank_state to 1 and, when engine_speed_limp_home_active_flag is 1 (speed limp home), calls cm848_exitSpeedLimpHome and re-runs engine_injectionTiming_crankSyncDispatch.
evidence: Read in full. The name is correct, not backwards: it tests the renamed flag in the right sense (leaves limp home when the primary crank input is back). It had no plate.

plate_comment: Run state transition handler: sets engine_crank_state.run_state to 1 and, when speed limp home is not active and crank_state is 4, calls cm848_enterSpeedLimpHome (backup speed input) and re-runs engine_injectionTiming_crankSyncDispatch.
evidence: Read in full. Name correct; the flag test (== 0 then enter) is right under the renamed polarity. It had no plate.

plate_comment: Run state 3 transition handler: snapshots crank_period_accumulator into crank_period_prev_snapshot, restarts engine_event_countdown from its calibration, sets run_state to 3, leaves speed limp home if it is active and re-runs engine_injectionTiming_crankSyncDispatch.
evidence: Read in full. Name correct under the renamed polarity. It had no plate.

plate_comment: Run state 4 transition handler: sets run_state to 4, leaves speed limp home (and re-runs engine_injectionTiming_crankSyncDispatch) only if it is active, and latches crank_tooth_period_tbl = TBLr - timebase_previous_capture the first time it is 0. cm848_engineRunState4Handler and ...Handler2 do the same but leave speed limp home unconditionally.
evidence: Read in full. Name correct ('Conditional' = the limp home exit is conditional). It had no plate.

plate_comment: Engine acceleration filter: engine_acceleration_unfiltered = change of engine_rpm_state.target_rpm since the previous call (6.25 rpm per second per count in the e2m), engine_acceleration_first_stage_filtered = first-order filter of it, clamped to engine_acceleration_first_stage_clamp_minimum .. _maximum (the filter accumulator is reset to the clamp value), engine_acceleration_second_stage_filtered = second first-order filter. Read by cm848_calculatePilotInjectionQuantity (pilot shutoff above an acceleration) and selectSensorRawChannels.
evidence: Read in full (28 lines). Name correct; it is the writer of the lead word 0x40b28e. The three consecutive words 0x40b28c / 0x40b28e / 0x40b290 match e2m Engine_Acceleration / Filtered_Engine_Acceleration / Unfiltered_Engine_Acceleration at 0x018A4300 / 02 / 04 (stage 1, stage 2, raw).

Resolves the wave-3 uncertain row. It is the main base timing command after the combustion limits and the calibrated override: written once per pass by cm848_selectFuelLimitOverride, read 3x by cm848_calculateMainInjectionTiming as the base term (sum / highest / lowest, source code 18). e2m block CBL (0x01171B00 = 0x40a466): CBL_SOI_Cmd +08 = 0x40a46e ('SOI command after imposing combustion limits'), CBL_SOI_Max_Limit +0A / CBL_SOI_Min_Limit +0C / CBL_SOI_Ref +0E = 0x40a470 / 472 / 474 and CBL_User_Incr_Flag +18 = 0x40a47e. RAM dump: 68 counts (7.97 deg) while the final main timing is 162.

Written once in cm848_calculateRpmLoadTables as the output of the second (maximum) engine speed x fuel_demand_limit_copy table, before the clamp; the clamp then keeps the result at or below it (fuel_demand_mode_code 27). e2m CBL_SOI_Max_Limit +0A. Dump 384 (> reference 68).

Output of the first table (0x40523e axis / 0x405266 axis / 0x405288 grid), used as max(minimum limit, reference); when it wins fuel_demand_mode_code = 28 (main timing source code 30). e2m CBL_SOI_Min_Limit +0C, and the two table triples follow the e2m min-then-max order. Dump 43. Not a fuel or load value: it feeds injection_timing_advance_calc, i.e. the main timing.

Result of the clamp max(minimum limit, reference + user increment) then min(maximum limit); read once by cm848_selectFuelLimitOverride. e2m CBL_SOI_Ref +0E ('SOI command after imposing combustion limits, before user override'). Dump 68 = the final command 68 (no override).

Written only in cm848_calculateRpmLoadTables: 0 when engine_feature_enable_flags bit 3 (8) is clear, otherwise (fuel_demand_mode_offset_cal != 0). e2m CBL_User_Incr_Flag +18 = 'TRUE if T_CBL_SOI_Increment_Enable is 1 AND C_CBL_SOI_Increment is not 0', the same expression. Read by cm848_setFuelStatusFlags (sets 0x10 of fuel_demand_mode_flags) and by cm848_updateMainInjectionTimingByDeliveryMode (rebuilds mask 4 of injection_timing_adjustment_flags; e2m Final_Timing_Adjustments_Flag order OFC, CBO, CBLINC, HPCRINC, CT, AIRT, AIRP, BST: the main timing code sets 0x10 / 0x20 / 0x40 / 0x80 for CT / AIRT / AIRP / BST and 8 for HPCRINC).

Copied into the base timing command by cm848_selectFuelLimitOverride when engine_feature_enable_flags bit 4 (16) is set. e2m C_CBL_SOI_Override_Value (0x01171A06, 'SOI override value in CBL algorithm'). Address 0x40523a is outside the EEPROM range 0x3fd482-0x3feec1, so no _cal suffix.

Added to the timing reference (fuel_correction_output_snapshot) when engine_feature_enable_flags bit 3 (8) is set, and its non-zero test sets the user increment flag. e2m C_CBL_SOI_Increment (0x01171A08, 'CPE User Commanded Timing Increment', CRANK_DEG_BTDC 0.1171875). Not a fuel demand offset. Outside the EEPROM range, so no _cal suffix.

Written at 0x15044 / 0x15054 in cm848_calculateFuelDemandTimingOffset, which looks up four engine speed x fuel_demand_limit maps (fuel_demand_calc_c / _b / _a / _boost5_lookup 0x40a4d4-0x40a4da) and picks / blends them by fuel_blend_lower / upper_map_number (the tail of that function was not read). cm848_applyFuelDemandOffset adds a table adjustment to it and clamps the sum to -1023..1024 counts (the same clamp as the main timing); the result is the timing reference that cm848_applyCombustionTimingLimits clamps. Two offset anchors against e2m block CBR at 0x0116A500 = 0x40a480: CBR_SOI_Ref +08 = 0x40a488, and CBR_SOI_Alpha1 / Chi2 / Chi3 / Chi4 +54..+5A = 0x40a4d4..0x40a4da. Dump 68 counts = the base command 68. Not an engine load.

cm848_applyFuelDemandOffset looks it up in engine_load_correction_axis_cal / _output_cal and adds it to the timing reference (sum clamped to -1023..1024 counts = fuel_correction_output); the active flag is (it != 0). e2m CBO_SOI_Ref_Adj +1C (CBO block 0x01171100 = 0x40a518; CBO_Delta_SOI +1E = 0x40a536, CBO_SOI_Adjust_Flag +20 = 0x40a538).

Written only by cm848_calculateFuelDemandDelta as clamp(engine_load_normalized - engine_load_normalized_prev, lower cal, upper cal): timing reference minus implemented main timing. e2m CBO_Delta_SOI ('Delta SOI input to off-nominal adjustment table'), +1E in its block; the clamp cals are C_CBO_Delta_SOI_Min / _Max.

Written only by cm848_applyFuelDemandOffset as (adjustment factor != 0). e2m CBO_SOI_Adjust_Flag +20 ('TRUE if CBO_SOI_Ref_Adj is not equal to zero'). Read by cm848_setFuelStatusFlags (sets 0x20 of fuel_demand_mode_flags) and by cm848_updateMainInjectionTimingByDeliveryMode (rebuilds mask 2 of injection_timing_adjustment_flags = e2m CBO).

Resolves the wave-3 uncertain row: the SNAPSHOT identification is right, the load name is wrong. Disassembly of engine_injectionAngle_updateCutoutAndTimingDemand: 0x527820 lha r29,-12158 (0x3fd082 = main_injection_timing_snapshot), 0x527828 sth -> 0x40b77c (main_injection_timing_for_cylinder_event), 0x527830 sth -> 0x40b31c; the only writer. The three readers use it as the implemented timing: cm848_calculateTimingReferenceDeltaAdjustment (reference minus it), cm848_auxiliaryControl_tableInterpolation (gain x (it - Alpha1 timing map output) = e2m SOI_Torque_To_Fuel_Adj, added to the total fueling), boost_targetPressure_loadRpm_calc (a term of the boost target). e2m: FSS_SOI 'interface from final timing to air handling code' at 0x018B3E12 = FSS block 0x018B3E00 (= 0x40b30a, FSS_Total_Fueling = engine_load_input_b) + 0x12 = 0x40b31c. Same block layout for the per-event words: 0x40b77c / 0x40b77e / 0x40b786 = FSS_Timing / FSS_Pilot_SOI / FSS_Aux_SOI (+0 / +2 / +A). Dump 0 (engine off); a copy of 0x40b77c.

Written only by cm848_processEngineRpmDerivative as engine_rpm_state.target_rpm - governor_target_rpm_snapshot (change of target rpm per call). e2m Unfiltered_Engine_Acceleration 0x018A4304 = +4 from 0x40b28c. Other readers (4 reads): cm848_processGovernorLoadCondition, cm848_processSpeedGovernorControl and cm848_updateTransmissionConditionFlags; they add it to a previous-snapshot copy and compare it with governor_speed_error_offset_cal, i.e. they use it as a rate of change (that cal and governor_speed_error_prev_snapshot are probably misnamed the same way; not checked).

cm848_processEngineRpmDerivative: first-order filter of the unfiltered change, clamped to +-94 counts (cals 0x40880c / 0x40880e). e2m Engine_Acceleration 0x018A4300 'after first stage low pass filtering' (6.25 rpm/s per count); the three words are consecutive like the three e2m words.

Resolves the wave-3 note: second first-order filter of the clamped acceleration (cm848_processEngineRpmDerivative, sole writer). e2m Filtered_Engine_Acceleration 0x018A4302 'after second stage low pass filtering'. Readers: cm848_calculatePilotInjectionQuantity (compared with the e2m Pilot_Shutoff_Acceleration cal, 'engine acceleration above which pilot is turned off') and selectSensorRawChannels. Dump 0 (engine off). Note the e2m lists 0.125 rpm/s for the cal but 6.25 for the variable it is compared with.

Names are swapped: cm848_processEngineRpmDerivative clamps the first-stage value DOWN to this word when it is larger (dump +94), so it is the maximum. Not a governor speed error; outside the EEPROM range, so no _cal suffix.
The first-stage value is raised to this word when it is smaller (dump -94), so it is the minimum, not an upper limit. Same function and reasons as 0x40880c.

cm848_updateEngineSpeedFromCrankSignal: engine_rpm_measured = crank_tooth_rpm, replaced by crank_derived_rpm when this flag is 0; set to 1 in speed limp home and in some crank_state / run_state combinations. crank_tooth_period_raw is the sum of the tooth periods captured in the channel 1 handler mpc555_updateEngineCrankState, so the flag reads as a speed source choice. Other readers: cm848_calculatePilotInjectionPulseWidth, cm848_calculateAuxiliaryInjectionPulseWidth (the wave-3 note says it chooses crank_tooth_period_raw or crank_period_accumulator; not re-checked), cm848_setMainQuantityAndPulseWidthLimits and cm848_vehicleSpeedSensorInterruptHandler (0x526f98, picks engine_rpm_state.reserved_0a or reserved_0c by the flag). It sits at e2m Speed_Sensor_Select ('source for speed calculations', ESSNSE) = Speed_Limp_Home (0x40b7d6) + 2. Dump 0.

Read by engine_injectionAngle_computeLoadCh6 and cm848_calculatePilotInjectionTiming: if engine speed < this word the duration word 0x4090eb is used, else 0x4090ed; the duration x crank angle per period gives the angle by which the TPU channel 6 wake-up position is moved earlier. e2m HPCR_TPU_Latency_Min_Engine_Speed (0x01805C01, 0.125 rpm). Dump 3200 = 400 rpm. The polarity in the code is: below the breakpoint 1700 us, at or above it 500 us (the e2m text says the TPU duration becomes active above the minimum speed, which is the reverse, so the names state the code's polarity).

x axis (engine speed) of the lookup in engine_injectionAngle_tpuUpdate that builds injection_end_limit_angle (0x40b854); e2m EOI_Limit_X_Axis (0x0181A000, RPM 0.125) / EOI_Limit_Y_Axis (0x0181A100, 'EOI limit as a function of engine speed'). The old name says cam angle correction; the result is the end-of-injection limit that forces the auxiliary event off. Array row word[8], rename only.
Data of the same 1-D lookup (7 values, one per axis breakpoint): the base end-of-injection limit versus engine speed (e2m EOI_Limit_Y_Axis, CRANK_DEG 0.0234375). Array row word[8], rename only.

Read by engine_injectionAngle_computeLoadCh6 (0x529304) and cm848_calculatePilotInjectionTiming (0x52d23c) when engine speed < injection_wakeup_duration_speed_breakpoint; multiplied by the crank angle per period into the channel 6 wake-up lead angle. Dump 4250 x 0.4 us = 1700 us. e2m HPCR_TPU_Latency_Dynamic_Wakeup_Duration (0x01805C03). Width: xref_addr.py says word (2 reads / 0 writes, lhz, odd address in the packed ROM block 0x4090e8). Outside the time-shared RAM range.

The other branch of the same two reads (0x529310, 0x52d248): used at or above the breakpoint. Dump 1250 x 0.4 us = 500 us. e2m HPCR_Regular_Dynamic_Wakeup_Duration (0x01805C05). Width: xref_addr.py says word (2 reads / 0 writes, lhz). Outside the time-shared RAM range.

text: Combustion manager cluster (next-wave lead, not renamed here). The 'fuel_demand' / 'engine_load' / 'fuel_blend' words at ROM 0x14000-0x17000 and 0x503000-0x507000 are the Cummins combustion manager chain of the e2m (CBR combustion reference -> CBO off-nominal compensation -> CBL combustion limits -> commands for start of injection, fuel, mass charge flow (airflow) and EGR fraction), in timing counts / quantities, not engine load. Offset anchors (e2m block = CM848 base); the ones also confirmed by the code or the RAM dump are CBL +08..+0E and +18, CBR_SOI_Ref and Alpha1..Chi4, CBO +1C / +1E / +20, CBP +02 / +04 / +08 / +0A, FSS +12 and the per-event words, the rest are offset matches only: CBR 0x0116A500 = 0x40a480 (+08 CBR_SOI_Ref = 0x40a488; +52..+5A Alpha0 / Alpha1 / Chi2 / Chi3 / Chi4 = 0x40a4d2 fuel_demand_timing_lookup, 0x40a4d4 fuel_demand_calc_c, 0x40a4d6 _b, 0x40a4d8 _a, 0x40a4da fuel_demand_calc_boost5_lookup: so the four maps selected by fuel_blend_lower / upper_map_number are Alpha1, Chi2, Chi3 and Chi4, and the dump value 4 means Chi4; +00 CBR_Gross_Fuel = 0x40a480 fuel_table_load_axis); CBO 0x01171100 = 0x40a518 (CBO_SOI_Ref +08 = 0x40a520 probably fuel_correction_output, CBO_SOI_Adj +16 = 0x40a52e fuel_demand_correction_scale, CBO_SOI_Ref_Adj +1C = 0x40a534, CBO_Delta_SOI +1E = 0x40a536, CBO_SOI_Adjust_Flag +20 = 0x40a538); CBL 0x01171B00 = 0x40a466 (+00 EGR_Frac_Cmd, +04 Fuel_Cmd, +06 MCF_Cmd = 0x40a466 / 46a / 46c, not checked; +14 CBL_MCF_Ref = 0x40a47a fuel_demand_load_rate_cap, +16 CBL_Density_MCF_Limit = 0x40a47c fuel_demand_load_rate_cap_snapshot, i.e. the 'load rate cap' is a mass charge flow limit); CBL calibrations 0x01171A00 = 0x405234 (+0 EGR_Frac_Override_Value = fuel_demand_high_limit_override_cal, +2 Fuel_Override_Value = fuel_timing_target_override_cal, +4 MCF_Override_Value = fuel_demand_rate_cap_override_cal, +6 / +8 = the two timing words renamed here); CBP 0x01177A00 = 0x40a54e (+02 SOI_Torque_To_Fuel_Adj = 0x40a550 fuel_demand_offset_load_delta_correction, +04 CBP_SOI_Torque_Adj_Gain = 0x40a552 fuel_load_offset_gain_rpm, +08 CBP_Adj_Total_Fueling = DAT_0040a556, +0A CBP_Combustion_Torque = DAT_0040a558 = the fuel-to-torque table result; 0x40a54e fuel_demand_blend_deviation_working is probably CBP_Net_Combustion_Torque); FSS 0x018B3E00 = 0x40b30a (+00 FSS_Total_Fueling = engine_load_input_b, which is 0 with the engine off; +12 FSS_SOI = 0x40b31c). The CBP clamp cals 0x405a9c / fuel_demand_offset_load_delta_correction_upper_limit are C_CBP_SOI_Torque_Adj_Min / _Max.

Next-wave names for the six combustion limit tables (arrays, word[N] rows in global_variables.csv; roles confirmed from the two cm848_dualAxisTableInterpolation calls in cm848_calculateRpmLoadTables: x = engine_rpm_state.current_rpm, y = fuel_demand_limit_copy; e2m order C_CBL_SOI_Min then Max; dump outputs 43 and 384): 0x40523e injection_timing_rpm_axis_cal -> injection_timing_combustion_minimum_limit_x_axis; 0x405266 injection_timing_load_axis_cal -> injection_timing_combustion_minimum_limit_y_axis; 0x405288 injection_timing_advance_yend_cal -> injection_timing_combustion_minimum_limit_grid; 0x4054e8 injection_timing_mode2_rpm_axis_cal -> injection_timing_combustion_maximum_limit_x_axis; 0x405510 injection_timing_mode2_ystart_cal -> injection_timing_combustion_maximum_limit_y_axis; 0x405532 injection_timing_mode2_yend_cal -> injection_timing_combustion_maximum_limit_grid (all outside the EEPROM range, so no _cal). Also the clamp cals engine_load_correction_lower_cal / _upper_cal (0x405a0c / 0x405a0e = C_CBO_Delta_SOI_Min / _Max) and the tables engine_load_correction_axis_cal / _output_cal (0x405a5c / 0x405a6c, e2m C_CBO_SOI_Ref_Adj_Table) and fuel_demand_correction_scale_axis_cal / _output_cal (0x405a7c / 0x405a8c, e2m C_CBO_Delta_SOI_Axis / C_CBO_SOI_Adj_Table) belong to the timing reference adjustment. Not renamed here (not traced to the end): fuel_demand_limit_copy 0x40a51c, fuel_correction_output* (0x40a05e, 0x3fa63c working), fuel_demand_lookup_working 0x3fa642 and fuel_demand_mode_code_prev_snapshot 0x3fa644 (time-shared range 0x3F9800-0x3FDB30: any change needs the boot-ROM user check).

Main timing source codes (struct field source_priority, cm848_calculateMainInjectionTiming) refined: 18 = the base command injection_timing_main_base_command is the winner with the clamped reference between the limits; 29 (0x1d) = the base command was held at the maximum combustion limit (fuel_demand_mode_code 27 from cm848_calculateRpmLoadTables); 30 (0x1e) = held at the minimum combustion limit (fuel_demand_mode_code 28). Dump: fuel_demand_mode_code = 25 (0x19), so neither 29 nor 30 is selected there. Together with the wave-3 note this replaces the old 'mode variants' wording.

Struct torque_limit_arb_t (structure_definitions.csv, base 0x0040a2f6): the first field source_priority is NOT part of the torque limit arbiter. It is the main injection timing source code (writes in cm848_calculateMainInjectionTiming, reads in cm848_calculatePilotInjectionTimingOffset / cm848_updateMainInjectionTimingByDeliveryMode, was cm848_updateEngineStatusFlags). The other three fields belong to cm848_selectTorqueLimit and its users: source_active 0x40a2f8 (11 writes in cm848_selectTorqueLimit; also read by cm848_selectFuelDemandSource, cm848_calculateEffectiveFuelLimit, cm848_updateProtectionStateMachine; written by cm848_initTorqueLimitDefaults and cm848_monitorConverterSlipAndFuelLimit), limit_source 0x40a2fa (8 writes in cm848_selectTorqueLimit, 2 reads in cm848_processTorqueLimitTiming) and fuel_minimum 0x40a2fc (22 reads / 16 writes across 7 functions). Proposal for a later type change (no struct_field rename given, the field name is right but the struct is wrong): move source_priority out into its own global main_injection_timing_source_code (word, 0x40a2f6) and make the struct start at 0x40a2f8. Not checked: what the other three fields mean beyond 'torque limit arbitration'.

Polarity fallout of the engine_speed_limp_home_active_flag rename, checked: the flag has 26 lines (code and plate text) in 18 functions (cm848_updateEngineSpeedFromCrankSignal, cm848_exitSpeedLimpHome, cm848_enterSpeedLimpHome, engine_injectionTiming_crankSyncDispatch, the run-state handlers 0x44cc8-0x44f0c, mpc555_updateEngineRunState, mpc555_updateEngineCrankState, mpc555_resetEngineTimingAccumulators, cm848_calculateAuxiliaryInjectionQuantityLimit, engine_injectionAngle_updateCutoutAndTimingDemand, engine_injectionAngle_tpuUpdate, the two injection schedulers, cm848_calculatePilotInjectionQuantity); every compare I read is in the right sense. The five run-state handlers had no plate (added above), only cm848_protectionOverrideEvaluator had a wrong name (renamed above) and engine_injectionTiming_crankSyncDispatch had a plate naming retired callees. The wave-3 lead that 'mpc555_updateSensorDiagnosticFlags' tests the flag is rejected: that name is the old name of 0x191a0 (now cm848_updateBoostFuelCorrectionSquaredAverage), which has no use of the flag. mpc555_updateEngineRunState / mpc555_updateEngineCrankState (the TPU-A channel 0 / 1 handlers) were not read in full; their plates in function_renames.csv are consistent with the flag use sites.
